business_problem: Stanford needed a campus-wide GPU platform that could support interdisciplinary AI research at production scale without forcing labs to depend on fragmented clusters, complex allocations, or external resources for large multi-node training jobs.
solution_summary: Stanford designed Marlowe as a DGX SuperPOD-based research platform that complements its Sherlock cluster and gives researchers a clear path from small experiments to large, non-preemptible training runs. The system uses DGX SuperPOD infrastructure with 248 NVIDIA Hopper GPUs, Base Command Manager for cluster provisioning and administration, and Quantum-2 InfiniBand networking so multi-node workloads can scale the way industry-scale model training requires. Researchers apply for access, begin with smaller jobs, and then expand to larger allocations as experiments mature, all on the same governed architecture. That shared platform has already supported work in world models, vision-language alignment, protein folding, and biological foundation models, and it gives Stanford a durable operating model for turning campus research ideas into repeatable, high-throughput AI programs.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD
solution_components.role: Provides the integrated cluster architecture behind Stanford's Marlowe research platform.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA Hopper GPUs
solution_components.role: Supply the GPU capacity researchers use for large-scale training, fine-tuning, and inference.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA Base Command Manager
solution_components.role: Handles cluster provisioning, administration, and day-to-day operational control for Marlowe.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA Quantum-2 InfiniBand
solution_components.role: Provides the high-speed interconnect that lets Stanford researchers scale jobs across hundreds of GPUs.

data_flow: Research datasets and training jobs move from Stanford labs into the Marlowe platform, where Base Command Manager provisions DGX resources and Quantum-2 InfiniBand connects multi-node runs across Hopper GPUs. Results then flow back into research groups for model evaluation, publication, and follow-on experimentation across the wider Stanford ecosystem.
business_outcome: Marlowe now supports more than 500 active research accounts, contributes to over 18 million GPU hours across Stanford's compute ecosystem each year, and enabled outcomes such as 90x faster Gaussian-splat fitting and publication-scale world-model research that previously would have been much harder to run on campus.
